articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks' (Digest No.088)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Overhead lines are very susceptible to faults because of the exposure of the system equipment to the extremes of weather and environmental conditions. Fault finding on 11 kV overhead lines is often extremely time consuming due to the remote locations and difficulty of access for personnel. The author investigates pole mounted fault passage indicators (FPI). The FPI is mounted on the pole some distance below the conductors. When a change in status of the magnetic field radiating from the overhead line conductor, caused by a downstream faults, occurs the FPI is triggered. The indicator enables quick identification of the passage of the fault.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: What can be done from a construction point of view? (power overhead lines)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Overhead lines, by their manner of construction, are exposed to the forces of nature which may cause them to fail. These external influences include temperature variations, mechanical forces, overvoltages, corrosion and pollution. The author looks at these external influences and puts forward solutions which may make the networks more reliable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of microelectronic instrumentation to improve distribution system reliability and reduce maintenance costs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The author describes an inexpensive digital recording unit which can be installed in primary distribution substations to provide continuous monitoring of the performance of the protection and switchgear. By connecting the recorder into a SCADA network the data can be made available for use in preventive maintenance programmes operating on the central plant database. Early identification of plant malfunction, combined with contact condition prediction, will lead to improved reliability whilst simultaneously reducing maintenance costs by eliminating unnecessary visual post fault inspection.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: In the past, overhead lines have been protected by the use of fuses. However fuses, being open to the elements, need regular maintenance and, when a fuse has operated, a field visit for replacement. A further disadvantage of fuses is that they cannot detect low levels of earth fault current. Using the new Reyrolle Protection GAC sectionaliser control relay, described by the authors, in conjunction with an SF/sub 6/ filled switch, it is possible to provide a sectionaliser with the following features: remote operation, including remote closure for switches equipped with a closing coil; earth fault capability, down to 0.5% of rating, and dead line detection down to 10% of setting.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The automatic sectionalising link (ASL) is finding increasingly wide usage on UK overhead distribution systems. The general practice is to retrofit the ASL into existing expulsion fuse mounts at the head of spur lines. It is shown that the ASL appears to be a viable proposition wherever outages due to nondamage faults are a significant problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: System faults on 11 kV networks must be disconnected quickly from the system by the next stage of protection. The fault current threatens the condition of the circuit breaker so by monitoring it the condition of the circuit breaker can be fairly accurately predicted. The author presents the Capenhurst current counter which measures every current that its circuit breaker interrupts, and displays and remembers a cumulative total of those currents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated actuator design with remote operation for pole-mounted air-break disconnectors
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The installation of large telecontrol schemes for the remote control of distribution networks can minimise the effects of faults. In order to achieve remote operation of 11 kV overhead networks to improve reliability to customers, an actuator with some form of energy store to operate pole-mounted disconnectors must be designed. The authors describe the design of the actuator, together with a micro-outstation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remote control of air break isolators and the application of automatic sectionalisers on overhead lines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: As part of the continuing search for means of improving supply security and, in the event of fault, supply restoration times, trials are currently taking place using new types of equipment for fault sectionalising and remote control on overhead networks in Midlands Electricity. Two separate sections of network have been chosen, one for the application of remotely operated air break isolators using an extension of the UHF radio telecontrol system and one in which auto sectionalising links, sometimes called smart fuses have been installed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radio communication techniques for control and indication on overhead networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Low power radio telemetry and trunked private mobile radio (PMR) meet all the criteria important to the electricity companies who wish to extend current SCADA systems into the rural networks. The author describes how low power radio and trunked PMR can be used for communications in rural automation schemes, especially for control and indication on overhead networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Overhead line fault current indicators-are they cost effective?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: 2.7 million customers in the UK are supplied from 11 kV overhead networks. On average, they lose their supply for about 4 hours each year compared with about 30 minutes for their counterparts in urban areas fed from underground cables. As these are average values, many customers living in rural areas will suffer from interruptions of much longer duration. Accurate and reliable indication of the fault position by fault current indicators will give quicker and simpler fault location, more rapid restoration of supply to affected customers, more efficient use of operational staff and reduced wear and tear on the system. The author looks at fault current indicators and also presents an economic assessment of their feasibility.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Non-damage fuse operations on 11 kV overhead lines
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The Electricity Research and Development Centre (ERDC) is investigating circuit breaker operations and fault current waveforms of 11 kV overhead lines in order to justify new protection methods which may be used in the future. The author looks at nondamage fuse operations including auto-reclosing and fuse operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Influence of fault handling techniques on supply security
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The rural Electricity Supply Board (ESB) distribution system consists of 5500 km of (arc suppressed) 38 kV network feeding 320 38/10 kV substations ranging in capacity from 2 MVA to 10 MVA. The rural 10 kV network is operated with its neutral isolated from ground and consists of more than 18000 km of three phase, three wire backbone lines which feed a network of more than 54000 km of two phase, two wire lines. A strategic decision has been undertaken to prevent and minimise outages. The author looks at neutral treatment and lightning prevention to prevent outages; prevention of transient faults; and causes and effects of permanent faults.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Further developments in distribution switchgear for overhead networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Continuous development has been taking place in switchgear for overhead distribution networks and the author gives an update on the position. Auto-reclosers, sectionalisers and system automation are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The triggered spark gap for lightning protection
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: The transient overvoltages caused by the effects of lightning on an overhead line distribution network can be damaging to the system equipment, costly to the supply authority carrying out the repairs and inconvenient to the customer suffering from a likely loss of power supplies. The author describes the 11 kV triggered spark gap which can be used to protect networks from lightning. It consists of a specially manufactured porcelain with a high potential, earth, and two auxilliary electrodes forming a four capacitance bridge. A single triggered spark gap on the centre conductor will cause the necessary flashover to earth.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated protection and auto-reclose control of source circuit-breakers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Improving Supply Security on 11 kV Overhead Networks
abstract: Because of its inherent advantages, future protection relays of all types will utilise the integrated protection technique. Increasingly more of the logical decision making and interlocking will be devolved down from manual central control room operator decision in favour of the 'black box' combined protection and control relay. Advances in semi-conductor technology are providing relay designers with greater computing power without the disadvantage of excessive power supply requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
